reports.description: Incident Type: Cryptocurrency Investment / DeFi Scam Description: I am reporting a cryptocurrency fraud involving a fake DeFi application operating under the name Cryptoweb3 / cryptoweb3.life. I have been approache my friend and she talked about smart contract trading and there is a guy who is going help with signals. She met this guy on a dating app and she met him once. This guy told her he built an algorithm and he monitors the market for buy and sell contracts. She sent me a referral url for a dApp. I was instructed to connect my on-chain wallet via a Web3 browser and deposit funds to participate in a smart contract investment. After depositing, the platform blocked withdrawals and claimed my account was under “risk review.” I was later asked to pay additional fees labeled as “tax,” “risk resolution,” and “withdrawal processing.” Despite complying, no withdrawal was ever processed. On-chain analysis shows funds were sent to externally owned wallet addresses that exhibit aggregation and laundering behavior consistent with crypto fraud. I believe this operation is ongoing and may affect other victims. I request investigation and coordination with exchanges for potential asset freezing.

reports.description: I got contacted by Emma with phone number +49 15211339701. We have had a nice confersation over a couple of days. Then she asked me if I would be interested in an online survey. So she provided me with login details and instructions how to finish 60 simple trading deals. Then she paid out and asked if I also wanted to try it. So I registered on https://sfaliorderjob.cc/login We connected our accounts. I was able to do the same thing as she did finish the 60 trading deals. I also was able to withdrawl. Then the next day we did the same again. She finished the operation and I did the same afterwards but after I finished the operation after several top up payments in order to finish the 60 deals, I was not able to withdrawl. I contacted the support and was told that I need to add funds in order to payout. That´s when I realised it´s a scam. Normally an exchange does not ask for additional funds for verification. Please help me to get my payments back.

reports.category: Job Scam: Learn and Report on Chainabuse
reports.description: In October 2025 I applied for what appeared to be a remote job opportunity on a site that presented itself as a legitimate recruiting page. The scammers operated at least two fraudulent domains related to this scheme: 1. https://www.netaporterjob.com/ — hosted on Wix.com (IP 34.149.87.45). 2. https://www.naporter.shop/#/ — hosted via Cloudflare, Inc. (IP 172.67.138.48, United States). After registering on the fraudulent site(s) I was contacted by individuals using WhatsApp and Telegram. They persuaded me to transfer funds in cryptocurrency as part of the “onboarding/payment” / deposit process described by the scammers.Financial transfers and losses (breakdown): BityBank — USD 14,751.79 Crypto — USD 24.401,13 Mercado Bitcoin — USD 5,403.33 Funds initially deposited into the wallets above were later routed to accounts on exchanges (which I have identified during my own investigation). The primary receiving exchanges/accounts where funds ended up are: BityBank, Crypto, and Mercado Bitcoin (values listed above). I have found associated accounts on LBank that received funds originating from Destination address: 1) Trou4EavgzEMoBp3V93LNaaiKY3Y3Rg5Cx 2) TeqiXhjxBXenG3wvA2YiyDwJTuw6jeioer Other relevant details / indicators:My initial support request to LBank was registered under ticket number W4VFPN, but since I am not a direct customer of LBank, I was informed that no assistance could be provided. However. I am now seeking your collaboration with law enforcement for the formal investigation that has been opened in Brazil (Police Report No. PP8152-1/2025). The fraudulent webpages are impersonating a legitimate recruiting/job listing appearance and were hosted on platforms/services with infrastructure in the United States. Scammers used messaging apps (WhatsApp and Telegram) to guide me through conversion of my funds into crypto and to provide transaction instructions. I possess screenshots of the web pages, chat histories, wallet addresses, and transaction confirmations. I also have the on-chain links above confirming movement of tokens from the deposit addresses to the destination wallets/exchanges.

reports.category: Fake Return Scams: Secure Your Crypto Investments
reports.description: Gilian Tran (alleged name), contacted me via LinkedIn wanting to talk about management strategies. After a week, she requested to change platforms to Whatsapp where she then started to discuss about investments. She took her time over months explaining a new blockchain AI finance equivalent to the dot com era of investment explosion. With initial small investments from another made up platform, she gave some returns. This platform quickly stopped and she pointed the way over to Neweraeducation.com which is a fake investment site where money goes in and they control the money going out. The withdrawal registration involves you giving up your wallet pass phrase and wallet address.Once this is received, they hold your money in ransom and ask that you deposit the same amount into your wallet for checks (all bs). Once money is in the wallet, they use a different software to activate your pass phrase and bypass your 2 step authorisation.

The individual claimed they had a very successful crypto investment strategy. They directed him to invest in crypto via a fake investment website mdexproex. Over the course of April through July 2025, he has lost a total of $2.1 million USD, representing my parent's life savings Funds were lost through a combination of crypto wallet withdrawals into the scammer’s address and direct wire transfers to both US and international-based bank accounts.
